# Pandamonium v1.0.47

The atomic updater now cleans up after itself: only the two newest rollback snapshots are kept, so a long-lived installation cannot fill its disk with update copies. This release also mounts the core Jarvis-OS protocol packs across every conversation surface.

## MAD-890 — Protocols 1/4: mount the core JOS pack across chat, agent, and voice with P7 trace

### Problem

The Jarvis-OS engine invariants and identity/constitution rules existed only in specification documents; nothing applied them at runtime, so chat, agent, and voice turns had no shared, versioned protocol layer.

### Implementation

A `protocols/` pack format (manifest with id, version, scope, domains, token budget, and enforcement plus a compact body) with a strict validated loader in `src/protocol_registry.py`. Two core packs mount in `agent_system_prompt()` after the constitution — one seam so every surface inherits them: `jos-p0-engine` (engine invariants) and `jos-p1-identity` (identity rules, precedence order, truth/evidence rules, slimmed to ~621 estimated tokens). Mounted `{id, version}` pairs are recorded per turn through JOS-P7 events, and under context pressure the rendered advisory block is stripped before input-budget trimming so protocol text never evicts tool evidence. A `protocol_layer_enabled` setting disables the layer and restores prior prompt composition.

### Product value and UI visibility

Every text, agent, and voice turn now follows the same versioned engine and identity rules, and each turn's trace records exactly which pack versions were mounted. Disabling the layer returns the previous behavior byte-for-byte. The rule set lives in Markdown packs that can be reviewed and versioned like code.

### Verification

Red-first tests cover rendering, malformed-pack diagnostics, the disabled state, trace recording, and the pressure-strip regression. The full Python suite passes (5,617 passed, 5 skipped) at this release.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

The layer is controlled by the `protocol_layer_enabled` setting; disabling it restores the exact prior prompt composition. Malformed packs fail visibly instead of being silently dropped. No data, schema, or authentication changes.

### References

- [Linear MAD-890](https://linear.app/madpanda3d/issue/MAD-890/protocols-14-mount-the-core-jos-pack-across-chat-agent-and-voice-with)
- [Feature PR](https://github.com/MADPANDA3D/Pandamonium/pull/74)

## MAD-896 — Updater: automatically keep only the last two rollback snapshots

### Problem

Every update created a full stopped-state rollback snapshot and nothing pruned them. The CT103 installation reached 100% disk with 35 snapshots (~9.5 GB), and the v1.0.46 update failed at final-version confirmation with `[Errno 28] No space left on device` before rolling back safely.

### Implementation

After a successful update and health check, the updater prunes its own `update-*` backup directories under the configured backup root, keeping only the newest two (`BACKUP_RETENTION = 2`). Scope is strictly the updater's snapshots: task snapshots, symlinks, stray files, and anything outside the backup root are never touched. Pruning is non-fatal — a delete failure never fails an update that already succeeded — and the just-created snapshot is always retained because it is the newest. The names removed are recorded in the update history entry as `pruned_backups`.

### Product value and UI visibility

Updates cannot slowly consume the whole disk anymore. The updater UI is unchanged; after an update the history retains two rollback points instead of an unbounded list. Operators with already-bloated installations can reclaim space immediately (as was done manually on CT103: ~24 GB freed).

### Verification

Deterministic tests exercise keep-2 ordering, non-update entries, symlinks, stray files, and the missing-root safe path. The full Python suite passes (5,617 passed, 5 skipped), and the updater browser spec passes (18/18). Live confirmation happens on the next CT103 update.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

Retention is fixed at the newest two snapshots; the current and previous release directories are managed separately and unchanged. Existing installations keep their current backups until their next successful update. No data, schema, or authentication changes.

### References

- [Linear MAD-896](https://linear.app/madpanda3d/issue/MAD-896/updater-automatically-keep-only-the-last-two-rollback-snapshots)
